prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1399; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer's narrative. On arrival at the scene in Baytown, Texas, I found two vehicles in a low-speed head-on collision in the eastbound lane. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the first vehicle and reported pain in the right shoulder following the impact. Driver 2 stated that their vehicle crossed the centerline during a lane change and struck the front of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 2 was able to explain the sequence clearly and did not contradict the account given by Driver 1. Two witnesses on the roadside independently described the same sequence, and photographs taken at the scene show damage to both front ends that is consistent with the impact described. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy for the vehicle involved. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of the same vehicle, though the exact seating position at the moment of impact was not fully clear from the statements taken. No prior damage to either vehicle was observed or reported. Whether the shoulder injury resulted from this collision has not yet been determined and will require medical follow-up. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued at the scene.
